facts.statement: The genus Belemnobatis was described by Thiollière in 1852.
The type species of the genus Belemnobatis is Belemnobatis sismondae.
Seven other species are known within the genus Belemnobatis.
facts.quote: subdivision: B. aominensis B. kermacki B. moorbergensis B. noviodunumensis B. stahli B. variablis B. werneri

facts.statement: Belemnobatis is an extinct genus of rays that lived during the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Belemnobatis is an extinct genus of rays from the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Belemnobatis might be a wastebasket taxon.
facts.quote: It is possible this genus is a wastebasket taxon.

facts.statement: Fossils of Belemnobatis have been found in Europe and Thailand.
facts.quote: It is known from many sites of both Jurassic and Cretaceous age throughout Europe and a single Asian occurrence in the middle Jurassic of Thailand.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Belemnobatis is the family Belemnobatidae.
Belemnobatis belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
Belemnobatis lived between 184.2 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Aptian (184.2 to 113.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Belemnobatis has been considered related to other Jurassic rays in the family Asterodermidae.
rejected.quote: It has been regarded as related to other Jurassic rays in the family Asterodermidae.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'related to other Jurassic rays in the family'
